headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 21 of the Tour de France 2026
subtext: It’s time for the final stage of the Tour de France, the final parade some may think… The different overall standings are more or less settled, but there’s still a major prize on the line with a prestigious stage win to grab in Paris. And the introduction of the Côte de la Butte Montmartre in 2025, repeated this year, brings exhilarating racing to cap off three weeks of action since the Grand Départ in Barcelona. After the route was adapted due to the exceptional circumstances caused by the wildfires currently affecting France, the riders are presented in Thoiry but the start is set in Paris, at 17:50. The winners of the Tour de France 2026 will be crowned at around 19:45.

headline: Change to the route of the final stage
subtext: As numerous wildfires are currently affecting France, particularly the Gironde region, emergency services are fully mobilized to combat the blazes, while internal security forces are working to secure the affected areas and protect the population. In light of this, the Ministry of the Interior has decided to redeploy a portion of the internal security forces initially mobilized to ensure security for the final stage of the Tour de France, in order to reinforce the response efforts in the areas affected by the wildfires. In the spirit of national solidarity with the affected regions and populations, it has been decided to adjust the route of the final stage between Thoiry and Paris. Read more

headline: A moveable feast
subtext: With the conclusion of the Tour de France 2026, Paris is a stage finish for the 116th time. It has been the final venue of every edition since the first Tour de France (1903), except for the 2024 summer, when the race concluded in Nice while Paris was the setting of the Olympic Games. The arrival on the Champs-Élysées was introduced in 1975. Today marks the 51st time the Tour finishes on this iconic avenue. The circuit with Côte de la Butte Montmartre was inaugurated in 2025. After several attacks by Tadej Pogacar, Wout van Aert took the stage win while the Slovenian claimed his fourth overall victory.

headline: Maillot Jaune
subtext: With the certainty that nobody could threaten his overall lead, Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) dedicated himself to securing the white jersey and a podium finish for his Mexican teammate Isaac del Toro yesterday at Alpe d’Huez. Today, the Slovenian asset to take his fifth Tour de France and enter a very select club along with Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault, and Miguel Indurain, the other holders of the record for most overall victories. Second yesterday, Remco Evenepoel (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) is also second in the overall standings, 6’26’’ behind Pogacar, while Del Toro trails by 9’42’’.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) all but sealed the green jersey yesterday with his victory in the intermediate sprint of Saint-Julien-Mont-Denis. The Dane has 527 points, while Jasper Philipsen (Alpecin-Premier Tech) has 445 points. That makes a gap of 82 points that can’t be closed today. Biniam Girmay (NSN) is set to complete the top 3 of the points classification with the 361 points he’s already claimed. Already the winner of the points standings at La Vuelta and the Giro, Pedersen will be the sixth rider to win it in all three Grand Tours. Today’s stage offers up to 75 points: 25 for the first rider at the intermediate sprint (Champs-Élysées, km 27.9) and 50 for the stage winner.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Sublimated by the higher summits of the Alps, Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) is set to win the polka-dot jersey for the second time in his career. As he did in 2024, the Ecuadorian climber attacked again and again in the final week of the race, and took the lead of the overall standings on stage 19 both times. And just as he did in 2024, Carapaz also wins the Super Combativity award. His breakaways in the mountains saw him take 156 KOM points, while Pogacar has 100. Valentin Paret-Peintre completes the top 3 with 99 points.

headline: White jersey
subtext: After an intense battle against Paul Seixas (Decathlon CMA CGM), Isaac del Toro (UAE Emirates XRG) all but sealed the deal yesterday as he gained almost 2 minutes on the French rising star en route to Alpe d’Huez. Del Toro is the second Mexican winner of the young riders standings, 39 years after Raul Alcala.Lenny Martinez (Bahrain Victorious) will complete the top 3 ahead of Juan Ayuso (Lidl-Trek).

headline: Team classification
subtext: Lidl-Trek took the lead of the overall team standings on day 4, when Mads Pedersen and Quinn Simmons finished first and second in Foix, and the German team stayed on top all the way to Paris despite the pressure from UAE Emirates XRG. Pogacar’s squad brought the gap down to under a minute ahead of the final week but their strength faltered. Lidl-Trek face the final stage with a margin of 36’57’’ on the Emirati team. Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe will complete the top 3 (+1h06’22’’).

headline: No win for France, Italy or Spain: a first in 302 Grand Tours?
subtext: France, Italy or Spain, the three countries that invented and host the Grand Tours, are still without a stage win in this Tour de France, the 302nd Grand Tour in history (113 Tours, 109 Giros, 80 Vueltas). If they don’t succeed in their last chance today, this will be the first Grand Tour without a win from the “founding fathers”. France have won stages every year at the Tour except for 1926 and 1999. Their last win on the final stage was in 2003, when Jean-Patrick Nazon sprinted to victory at the Champs-Élysées. Italians won two stages last year with Jonathan Milan but they have not finished in a stage top-3 this year. Their last win in Paris came from Daniele Bennati in 2007. Spaniards are winless since Carlos Rodriguez’s success on 15 July 2023 (Morzine). Their only win on the final stage was in 1955, when Miguel Poblet covered the last 10 kilometres alone.

headline: Quinn Simmons has been named Best Teammate
Stage 21 of the Tour de France 2026 is ON!
subtext: The peloton just set off on the Champs-Élysées.

headline: For one last time this year
23 teams: the report cards
subtext: After 20 stages in the 113th edition of the Tour de France and before the prestigious final day, which is unlikely to shake up the various rankings, letour.fr takes a look at the highs and lows experienced by each of the 23 teams that set off from Barcelona on 4 July. While the riders start the stage and celebrate reaching Paris, we’ll publish their balance sheets in the reverse order of the team standings.

headline: The report card / Picnic PostNL: A blank slate
subtext: Having last claimed victory with Romain Bardet in Rimini in 2024, and now without Oscar Onley – who moved to Netcompany Ineos after a brilliant fourth place overall last year – Team Picnic PostNL arrived with the ambition of securing “stage results”. Their sprinter, Pavel Bittner, was one of their strongest assets, whilst Warren Barguil and John Degenkolb were counting on their experience to make a difference in a squad that fielded four newcomers to the Tour de France. The Frenchman and the German went on the attack on several occasions, alongside Robbe Dhondt in particular, to launch breakaways. But their efforts did not bear fruit. In the end, the team secured just one top-10 finish in the bunch sprint at Bergerac, where Bittner took 5th place, achieving the Dutch team’s best result.

headline: The report card / NSN: On the brink of victory
subtext: The NSN team arrived with the aim of helping their sprinter, Biniam Girmay, return to winning ways, two years after his last victory in the Tour de France. The Eritrean was well supported, taking part in all five bunch sprints (stages 5, 7, 8, 11 and 12). However, he failed to claim victory, finishing 3rd in Bordeaux and then 2nd in Bergerac, and was also unable to reclaim the green jersey he had won in 2024. The other most active NSN riders were George Bennett, Lewis Askey and Marco Frigo. The latter two showed good instincts by taking part in winning breakaways, though neither was the rider to seal the victory in these attacks: Frigo finished fourth in Foix, as did Askey in Voiron.

headline: The report card / Cofidis: Missed opportunities
subtext: A year on from a relatively lacklustre Tour, the French team was hoping to turn things round with a new line-up, as the riders behind the two top-10 finishes in 2025 – Bryan Coquard and Dylan Teuns – were not there. A newcomer to the Tour de France, Belgian sprinter Milan Fretin secured two top-five finishes at Nevers (4th) and Chalon-sur-Saône (5th). Luxembourg’s champion Alex Kirsch and France’s Hugo Page were among the most active riders when it came to launching breakaways, though they failed to convert this into a major result. Ion Izagirre also tried his hand at attacking. The experienced Spaniard finished his final Tour de France in a modest 45th place in the general classification, as the team’s best-placed rider.
